title: Scientific Literacy & Data Analysis
description: Develop the vocabulary and structures needed to discuss scientific data, interpret statistical results, and engage in evidence-based arguments. Learn to read, analyze, and communicate scientific information effectively in Spanish.

grammar.title: Expressing Data Interpretation and Scientific Claims
grammar.content: At B2.1 level, you need to articulate how data should be interpreted, distinguish between correlation and causation, and express scientific claims with appropriate certainty levels.

rows: Stating a finding
Los datos muestran que... / Los resultados indican que...
Los datos muestran que hay una correlación entre ambos factores.
Expressing uncertainty
Es posible que + subj. / Podría ser que + subj.
Es posible que los resultados se deban a otros factores.
Distinguishing correlation/causation
Correlación no implica causalidad
La correlación entre X e Y no implica causalidad.
Qualified conclusion
Se puede concluir que... / Parece que...
Se puede concluir que hay una tendencia significativa.
Hedging a claim
En general / Por lo general / En la mayoría de los casos
En general, los datos apoyan la hipótesis.
Refuting evidence
Sin embargo / No obstante / Por el contrario
Los datos sugieren X; sin embargo, otros estudios indican Y.

examples: Los datos muestran que hay una correlación entre el consumo y los resultados.
Es posible que los resultados se deban a otros factores.
La correlación entre X e Y no implica causalidad.
Se puede concluir que hay una tendencia significativa.
Los datos sugieren X; sin embargo, otros estudios indican Y.
grammar.aid_note: Romanian speakers: Romanian uses similar hedging — datele arată că ≈ los datos muestran que, este posibil ca ≈ es posible que. The structure corelația nu implică causalitatea maps directly.

grammar.title: Subjunctive in Scientific Discourse
grammar.content: Scientific writing requires expressing doubt, possibility, and evaluation of evidence — all of which trigger the subjunctive in Spanish.

rows: Doubt about findings
No es concluyente que + subj. / No se sabe si + subj.
No es concluyente que los resultados sean definitivos.
Evaluative judgment
Es importante que + subj. / Es esencial que + subj.
Es importante que se reproduzcan los experimentos.
Possibility
Es probable que + subj. / Puede ser que + subj.
Es probable que haya sesgo en la muestra.
Requirement
Es necesario que + subj. / Hay que + inf.
Es necesario que se controle la variable dependiente.
Purpose
Para que + subj. / A fin de que + subj.
Para que los resultados sean válidos, se necesita una muestra representativa.

examples: No es concluyente que los resultados sean definitivos.
Es importante que se reproduzcan los experimentos.
Es probable que haya sesgo en la muestra.
Es necesario que se controle la variable dependiente.
Para que los resultados sean válidos, se necesita una muestra representativa.
grammar.aid_note: Romanian speakers: Es probable que haya sesgo ≈ Este posibil să existe bias. Romanian să + conjunctiv maps to Spanish que + subjuntivo.

pronunciation.title: Stress Patterns in Scientific Vocabulary
pronunciation.content: Scientific Spanish vocabulary contains many esdrújulas and agudas with written accents.

examples.source: ee-poh-TEH-sis (llana, no accent — note: sis with s)

pronunciation.aid_note: Romanian speakers: Spanish c before e and i sounds like th in Spain or s in Latin America. The Spanish r in experimental is a single tap, not rolled.

exercises.question: What does la correlación no implica causalidad mean?
options: Correlated events always cause each other
Just because two things are correlated does not mean one causes the other
Correlation is more important than causation
exercises.explanation: One of the most important principles in statistics: correlation between two variables does not mean one causes the other.

exercises.question: Which structure appropriately expresses a cautious scientific conclusion?
exercises.explanation: Science requires caution: En general, los datos sugieren... expresses a conclusion based on evidence without absolute claims.

exercises.question: Complete: Los datos muestran que _____ una correlación entre ambos factores. (The data shows that there is a correlation between both factors.)
exercises.explanation: Los datos muestran que hay... — the verb haber in 3rd person singular to indicate existence.

exercises.question: Which of these is NOT a type of variable in an experiment?
exercises.explanation: Variable aleatoria is a probabilistic concept, not an experimental variable type. Experimental variables are independent, dependent, and control.

exercises.question: Complete: Es probable que haya _____ en la muestra. (It is likely there is bias in the sample.)
exercises.explanation: Hay sesgo en la muestra — sesgo is the technical term for bias in Spanish scientific context.

exercises.question: What does significancia estadística mean?
options: That the result is not due to chance
That the result is very large
That the result is socially important
exercises.explanation: Statistical significance means results are unlikely to have occurred by chance, usually with a p-value < 0.05.

exercises.question: Complete: _____ que se reproduzcan los experimentos. (It is important that the experiments be reproduced.)
exercises.explanation: Es importante que + subjunctive — reproduzcan is subjunctive of reproducir in 3rd person plural.

exercises.question: Which phrase is correct for expressing scientific uncertainty?
options: Es posible que los resultados se deban a otros factores.
exercises.explanation: Es posible que + subjunctive expresses appropriate uncertainty in scientific context.

exercises.question: Complete: Para que los resultados _____ válidos, se necesita una muestra representativa. (For the results to be valid, a representative sample is needed.)
exercises.explanation: After para que, use the subjunctive: sean (subjunctive of ser in 3rd person plural).

exercises.question: Which structure correctly compares data?
options: En comparación con, los datos muestran...
exercises.explanation: En comparación con... is the appropriate structure for comparing results or data in scientific context.
